title: Grateful Dead Live at Musikhalle on 1972-04-29
source: Source: Unknown mics > Uher 4400 > Master Reel > PCM > DAT (44.1k) - Taped by Wolsander* and provided by Tim Dalton; Tansfer: Dat > Sony PCM-R500 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/44.1 - Transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: Wav > Adobe Audition 3 > iZotope RX 6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave > Flac 16; edited and mastered SIRMick May 2018

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience‑sourced recording of the legendary Hamburg 1972 concert, noted for its crystal‑clear PA sound and an unforgettable, marathon performance.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about this April‑29‑1972 Hamburg show as one of the best they’ve ever seen, with a lengthy set that ran past midnight until the venue cut power. The AUD source captures the hall’s PA beautifully—low crowd ambience, crisp clarity, and a sound quality that rivals Bear’s board recordings. Although the second encore of "Uncle John's Band" is missing from the tape, the overall listening experience is highly praised.

ai_rating.rationale: High praise for both performance and recording quality across two reviews, but limited sample size reduces confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Balcony‑rail microphones provide low crowd cheer ambience and exceptionally clear PA sound; reviewers describe the audio as a 'real treat' with superb hall acoustics, comparable to soundboard recordings.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Marathon set that started at 8 PM and ran well beyond midnight; the band kept the energy high until venue staff shut off power, making it a legendary night.
